newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: BEST OFFER FOR TAIWAN SEPT REFORMATE OVER $24/BBL.
newsitem.headline: BEST OFFER FOR TAIWAN SEPT REFORMATE OVER $24/BBL.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) has received nine offers over $24.00 per barrel in its 95-octane unleaded reformate import tender for September, a company official said on Tuesday.
"The numbers are still not so good," he said on the tender which seeks the cargo for delivery to Keelung, Kaohsiung, Shalung or Taichung on a cost-and-freight (c+f) basis.

CPC's tender for September 1-30 delivery which closed on August 11 and is valid for two days, is a re-issue of an earlier tender for the first half of September which was cancelled due to high offers.
The official did not specify how much higher above $24 the best offer was.
"We will counter the price with the majors and traders," he said. "If we can get $24.10 or $24.20, we will consider it."
He said the offer level was too high considering the published Singapore free-on-board quotes at $22.55 and the freight to Taiwan around $1.30 per barrel.
He said CPC received nine offers, four of which were from majors.
CPC, which normally buys at least two 250,000-barrel cargoes monthly, has not purchased any September delivery barrels so far.
If the sellers do not lower their offers, CPC "may buy only one cargo or maybe cancel," the official said.
The last tender was cancelled as the best offer was "too high" at around $25.30.
In August, CPC bought three cargoes, two for Aug 1-10 delivery at around $24.60-$24.76 and one for Aug 11-20 at $23.30, c-and-f Taiwan.
